To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we provide a method for estimating the flow distribution from sampled flow statistics, 2) we demonstrate that our method works for different types of sampling, 3) we show that the method can be improved by taking advantage of protocol level details in flow records, and 4) we show that our method can be improved when the flow records contain packet level information.

(i) we can infer flow distributions with high accuracy; (ii) the accuracy of the inference depends on the number of flows sampled, but not the sampling rate; and (iii) we can use the results to predict the distribution of flow durations, which is useful for traffic engineering and for estimating network resource usage.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of how much can we infer about the characteristics of unsampled flows from the flow statistics of a sampled stream.
the following question: Given sampled flow statistics from a stream of network traffic, what can we say about the unsampled flow statistics?
the question: How much of the traffic is missing?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the methods we propose can be applied to sampled flow records to infer the distribution of packet counts per flow in the original traffic.
sampling does not significantly affect the accuracy of the inferences we draw, provided that the sampling rate is high enough.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we can estimate the flow statistics of unsampled traffic from sampled traffic with reasonable accuracy.

the packet sampling process does not significantly distort the distribution of the number of flows in the sampled stream, and that the number of flows can be inferred from flow statistics in the sampled stream.
we can infer a flow distribution from a sampled flow distribution, and we can infer a sampled flow distribution from a packet sampled distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to infer the flow distribution from a sample of flow statistics, even when the sampling rate is as low as 0.1%.
, even with sampling rates as low as 0.1%, we can estimate the number of packets in the original stream with high accuracy.
, even when sampling is used, the statistics of flows can be estimated from a small sample of packets.
